stories.label: Houthi missile threat towards Riyadh causes damage, Saudi-led coalition says, as Houthis advance on Aden
stories.summary: Debris from a Houthi missile fell in Riyadh after a loud boom over the Saudi capital, while on the ground Houthi forces push toward Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government, and the coalition strikes military sites. Lead with the two fronts at once: the war has reached the Saudi capital and the south's last stronghold in the same day. Name who lives in Aden's path and what a fall would mean for shipping through Bab el-Mandeb.

stories.label: Israel forces kill 3 Palestinians in fresh Gaza push
stories.summary: New development since our central-Gaza ground-operation story: the Board of Peace has issued a report warning the ceasefire faces imminent collapse and blaming both Israel and Hamas, while Israeli tanks pushed further into central Gaza and killed three Palestinians. Lead with the report and the deaths together: the body meant to guarantee the truce splits the blame while one side's tanks are advancing. Name the three killed if sources do, and give Hamas's charge that the board is 'protecting Israel'.

stories.label: Kuwait, Bahrain face new Iran attacks after US strike on Qeshm Island
stories.summary: After the US bombed Qeshm Island, Iran's base at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran hit an airbase used by US forces in Kuwait and struck Bahrain several times. Peace talks are stalled. Lead with the cycle: each US strike now brings Iranian fire on the Gulf states that host US forces, so their own populations take the risk. Mention ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: French centrists and conservatives struggled to gain ground
stories.summary: Polls point to a runoff between Marine Le Pen's far right and Jean-Luc Mélenchon's hard left. Édouard Philippe launched his programme on Wednesday, and the centre that has governed France since 2017 cannot break through. Lead with what that runoff would mean for the euro zone's second-largest economy, its debt and its Ukraine policy, and use the candidates' clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage as the mechanism.

stories.label: Army comments on viral video, admits dialogue with terrorists in Kwara
stories.summary: Nigeria's army, which publicly rules out negotiating with bandits, has confirmed that its troops held talks with armed groups in Kwara State. It did so only after videos of soldiers mingling with the gunmen went viral. Lead with that gap between policy and practice. Name who pays for it: villagers in north-central Nigeria, where kidnapping for ransom has spread south from the northwest, and who get no say in local deals with the men who raid them.

stories.label: Fed's Daly Urges Rate Hikes With a Thoughtful, Measured Approach
stories.summary: The minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting show 'almost all' officials saw a growing risk that they will have to tighten further, even as they held rates. San Francisco Fed president Mary Daly now openly calls for hikes. Lead with the shift from 'hold' to 'when to raise' and with its cause, an inflation pushed up by the oil shock. Show who carries the cost: borrowers worldwide whose dollar debt reprices. Name the series: the Fed funds rate, US inflation and the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: In Focus | Sign of the times? How China is quietly shifting global trade onto yuan payments
stories.summary: China now settles nearly 30% of its trade in yuan, and the push comes from exporters crowding branches like VTB's in Shanghai as well as from Beijing. Lead with the 30% figure and with the mechanism: sanctions on Russia and Iran made dollar payments a risk, so traders route around them. Name what this means for countries that sell to China under US sanctions. Name the series: the yuan against the dollar.

stories.label: 'We call it a sea bible' -- the West Coast fishers reading an ocean
stories.summary: Small-scale fishers in Port Nolloth and Doringbaai on South Africa's West Coast are in court against TotalEnergies' plan to drill offshore. Lead with the court challenge: a French oil major's licence against communities whose crayfish catch and inherited knowledge of the sea are their whole livelihood. Report the court's timeline and what the fishers argue. This is the case, not a feature about the town.

stories.label: 奇袭GPT-6.2！谷歌迄今最强Gemini登场，7周内第四发，RSI时代真来了
stories.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth Gemini 4 model in seven weeks. It ranks third on the Artificial Analysis index and costs $3/$15 per million tokens, which Google puts at 50-80% below rival frontier models per task. Lead with the pace and with the price war: frontier capability is getting cheaper faster than labs can differentiate. Add the self-improvement memory (SIM) paper Google cites, and a cyber variant opened only to vetted defenders.

stories.label: Q3营收重返正增长，不卷外卖的京东将“拐”向何方？
stories.summary: JD.com's revenue is growing again in the third quarter after the company pulled back from China's subsidy war over food delivery. Lead with the retreat: one of China's largest platforms is cutting non-core spending and going back to supply-chain efficiency, because e-commerce has become a fight over a market that has stopped growing. Give the Q3 figures and what the end of cash-burn growth means for Meituan and Alibaba.

stories.label: Bitcoin miner that sold its last BTC warns it may run short of cash for $1.2 billion AI deal
stories.summary: A listed bitcoin miner sold its whole bitcoin treasury to become an AI data-centre host, and now warns it may run out of cash before finishing the build. The headline $1.2 billion contract depends on two five-year extensions. Lead with that fragility: the miners-to-AI pivot rests on contracts that are mostly options. Name the company and its filing. Name the series: bitcoin.

stories.label: US Pentagon chief Hegseth signs military deal in Venezuela
stories.summary: Ten months after a US raid toppled Maduro, Hegseth is in Caracas signing a deal to re-establish military ties with Delcy Rodríguez's government. Lead with the reversal — 'from our most...' adversary to partner — and ask what Washington gets (bases, access, the Orinoco oil deal from 11 November) and what Venezuelans gave up in sovereignty.

stories.label: “I Didn’t Expect Jenin Could Change So Much”: Reporter Jailed for Nearly 2 Years on Israel’s Destruction
stories.summary: Palestinian journalist Mujahed Al-Saadi spent 22 months in Israeli prison and came home to an emptied Jenin refugee camp, flattened by Operation Iron Wall. Lead with what he found; the mechanism is a camp of thousands depopulated while attention was on Gaza, and a reporter held so long he could not report it. Continuation of displacement is the story.

stories.label: El último control sobre el TSE opera excluido y sin recursos rumbo a elecciones 2027
stories.summary: El Salvador's Junta de Vigilancia Electoral, the last independent check on the electoral tribunal, is shut out of its work and left without funds ahead of the 2027 elections, while the tribunal's president collects an award for 'strengthening democracy'. Lead with that contrast; the mechanism is how Bukele's system hollows out oversight without abolishing it.

stories.label: Norm Coleman: Hegseth adviser double-dipping for Israel, Saudi
stories.summary: Co-published with The Guardian and built on lobbying disclosures: Norm Coleman sits as vice chair of the Pentagon's Defense Policy Board while registered as a lobbyist for Saudi Arabia and serving as senior adviser to Israeli weapons firm Kinetica, which says US-Israel defence integration is its business thesis. Lead with the three hats; the mechanism is the Federal Advisory Committee Act loophole that bans individual lobbyists but not lobbyists working through a firm. Attribute claims to the reporting.

stories.label: Países europeus adotam “modelo Trump” e criam centro de deportação em Ruanda
stories.summary: European governments are setting up a deportation centre in Rwanda to hold people they expel, the offshore model the US used. Report the facts, not the column's tone: which countries, who is sent, what Rwanda is paid, and what legal status the deportees have. The structural point is Europe paying an African state to warehouse people it will not keep.

stories.label: Pakistan's mango exports fall 36pc amid US-Iran war: exporters' association
stories.summary: Pakistan exported 78,000 tonnes of mangoes this year, down 36%, because the US-Iran war cut Gulf shipping routes and drove freight costs up. Lead with the farmers and exporters in Sindh and Punjab paying for a war they are not in; mechanism is the Gulf as Pakistan's nearest market and transit hub. Chart: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: IMF forecasts Qatar’s economy to shrink by more than 14% in 2026
stories.summary: The IMF now expects Qatar's economy to contract by more than 14% this year, a depression-scale fall for the world's richest LNG exporter, as the Iran war shuts Gulf shipping. Lead with the number; the mechanism is an economy that depends on tankers leaving through Hormuz. Chart: natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: German judge proposes dropping Movie2k case if operator hands over $2.56 billion in bitcoin
stories.summary: A German court has offered to drop the money-laundering case against the alleged Movie2k piracy operator if he surrenders 40,000 bitcoin (about $2.56bn) and €38m. Lead with the bargain — the state buying a fortune instead of a verdict — and the precedent of settling crypto crime by confiscation. Chart: bitcoin.

stories.label: Judge signs off on sale of Spirit Airlines’ data to Google
stories.summary: A bankruptcy judge let Google buy defunct Spirit Airlines' customer data for $10m to use in AI projects. Lead with the precedent: passengers' records, given to an airline, sold as a bankruptcy asset to train AI. Name the protections Google agreed to and what they leave out.

stories.label: Games-Branche: Arbeitskampf bei GTA VI
stories.summary: GTA VI, one of the biggest games ever made, launches tomorrow while the people who built it are fighting Rockstar in court and inside the company over union organising. Lead with that timing; the mechanism is crunch and firings in a sector that has resisted unions, and why this case matters beyond one studio.

stories.label: 股价回撤近八成后抛9.5亿定增，欧科亿的逆周期扩张赌局
stories.summary: Chinese carbide-tool maker OKE Precision (欧科亿), its shares down nearly 80%, is raising ¥950m in a private placement to expand capacity as the tungsten-price windfall fades. Lead with the counter-cyclical bet; the structural why is China's grip on tungsten, the metal in every cutting tool and armour-piercing round, and what happens to its processors when prices turn.

stories.label: NIH to move last group of its research chimps to a sanctuary
stories.summary: The last chimpanzees the US government owns that still live in a lab will move to Chimp Haven next year, more than a decade after NIH ended funding for biomedical chimp research. Lead with how long the retirement took and why; the science point is what the end of chimp research did to the work that depended on it.

stories.label: Training gaps threaten fistula care in rural Liberia
stories.summary: Health workers in rural Liberia say they are not trained to recognise obstetric fistula, so women with a curable injury of childbirth are never referred for surgery. Lead with the women left incontinent and shunned for want of a diagnosis; the mechanism is a referral chain that breaks at the first clinic.

stories.label: Inside Nigeria's illegal gold mining industry
stories.summary: Most of Nigeria's gold, lithium and uranium is mined illegally, so billions of euros never reach national accounts. Two years after Abuja launched a clean-up of the sector, lead with how much still escapes and who controls it: armed groups, foreign buyers, or licensed fronts. Contrast with Egypt's shift (covered 11-18) from crackdown to buying from informal miners. Name gold. Dateline Abuja unless the source reports from a mining state such as Zamfara or Niger.

stories.label: Iran's IRGC says two tankers ablaze in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC says two more tankers are burning in the Strait of Hormuz, after Mehr reported a fourth tanker mined, while a senior US Navy official told senators that insuring a single transit now costs $64m, contradicting Trump's claim the strait is open. Lead with the $64m premium: mines, not blockades, are what is emptying the strait. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Attribute the IRGC claim; the Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye reporting is independent.

stories.label: El Salvador Destroys Another Gang Stronghold as 'Gift' to Haiti
stories.summary: Bukele's forces fired helicopter missiles at another Haitian gang leader's stronghold and posted the video as a 'gift', while thousands marched in Port-au-Prince in support of the Salvadoran troops. Lead with the two at once: a foreign army waging an air war in a capital, cheered by people the UN mission failed, and the question nobody is answering of who counts the civilians under the missiles and under what law.

stories.label: Israel launches ground operation in central Gaza; Jeffries wins speaker nomination; NSA’s internal comms system goes down
stories.summary: Take only the lead item: Israel has launched a ground operation in central Gaza. Lead with where the troops went, who lives there and how many were killed or displaced, with names and numbers, not 'clashes'. Ignore the Jeffries and NSA items in the same newsletter.

stories.label: ICJ report sees 'judicial capture' in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
stories.summary: The International Commission of Jurists (the Geneva jurists' body, not the court in The Hague) finds that Pakistan's 26th and 27th amendments produced 'systemic judicial capture': constitutional benches carved out of the Supreme Court, with judges picked by a commission the government controls. Lead with the mechanism, who picks the judges now, and what cases those benches have since decided.

stories.label: EU Proposes €45 Billion Loan For Ukraine, Kyiv To Repay Only After Russian Reparations
stories.summary: The European Commission proposes a €45bn loan to Ukraine that Kyiv repays only if Russia pays reparations. Lead with that condition: in practice the loan is a grant, or a bet on Russian money, and the mechanism to explain is what backs it (the frozen Russian assets) and which member states must agree.

stories.label: Extradited, Cooperated, Released: How US Courts Recycle Drug Traffickers.
stories.summary: Guatemala has re-arrested Horst Walther Overdick, 'El Tigre', a trafficker the US extradited, convicted and then released after he cooperated. Lead with the cycle: plea deals trade information for short sentences, and the men go home to the same trade, so the atrocities in Guatemala go unpunished while Washington counts a conviction. Dateline Cobán.

stories.label: UAE top destination for smuggled African gold despite tighter measures, NGO says
stories.summary: Swissaid finds the UAE took in an estimated 413 tonnes of smuggled African gold in 2024, still the top destination a year after Dubai tightened its rules. Lead with the tonnage and what it costs the African states it leaves (Sudan, Mali and others), and why due-diligence rules on paper have not stopped it. The gold price is the series.

stories.label: How Paris and Berlin sealed the ECB succession
stories.summary: Germany has nominated Princeton's Markus Brunnermeier for the ECB board, and euro-zone finance ministers extended the deadline for the chief economist and market-operations posts to November 20. Lead with the deal: France and Germany are dividing the seats that set euro-zone rates and run its bond purchases, the ones that decide how hard markets can press on French debt. The ECB rate is the series.

stories.label: Europe EV sales jump in October as high oil prices, subsidies fuel demand
stories.summary: Battery-electric car registrations in Europe rose more than 60% year on year in October, to about a third of new cars. Lead with the cause: the Gulf war's oil shock is doing what years of climate policy did not, with subsidies and cheaper models on top. Name the series: Brent crude.

stories.label: Heimlicher Zugriff auf Fahrzeugdaten: Die Auto-Branche als verlängerter Arm der Geheimdienste
stories.summary: German carmakers are now obliged to hand telemetry, sensor and behaviour data on drivers and passengers to the intelligence services on request, secretly. Lead with that the car is now a surveillance device by law, and with the gap the industry itself points to: no one has said which data is covered.

stories.label: 资本开支暴涨528%！腾讯继续加码AI，WorkBuddy登顶国内AI用量第一
stories.summary: Tencent's Q3 capital spending rose 528% to 81.4bn yuan, free cash flow went to -69bn on 86bn of prepaid compute, and new AI products cut 15.2bn from operating profit. President Martin Lau says the latest chip import curbs cut usable compute and will delay the next Hunyuan model. Lead with the chip curbs biting, and with his answer: domestic chips and a model 95% cheaper to run.

stories.label: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
stories.summary: ULA says Sunday's Vulcan failure on the Leo 1 launch came from inadequate fuel supply to its Blue Origin BE-4 engines. Lead with the shared engine: the same BE-4 flies on New Glenn, so one fault grounds both heavy rockets the US set up as SpaceX's alternatives, and the Amazon Leo constellation with them.

stories.label: Bolivia's Madidi National Park shelters 99 bat species, including 7 new to the country
stories.summary: A survey confirms 100 bat taxa in Madidi National Park, including seven new to Bolivia and one that may be new to science: 68% of Bolivia's known bat species in one park. Lead with that concentration, and with what the bats do for the forest (pollination, seed dispersal, insect control) in a park under pressure from roads, mining and dams.

stories.label: Why is SPDR Gold Shares sliding today? By Investing.com
stories.summary: New development past our 11-16/11-17 gold stories: spot gold has broken lower again, to its weakest since September 2025, after Fed governor Christopher Waller urged a half-point rate hike in December and markets now price a December hike at about 96% ahead of today's October minutes. Lead with the mechanism: a Fed that turns to hiking pulls the dollar up and makes a non-yielding metal costlier to hold. Then who it lands on: central banks that bought gold to escape the dollar, and households in India and Turkey who save in gold. Chart gold and the US 10-year Treasury yield. No US dateline needed — dateline the market move to London or Mumbai.

stories.label: Man sentenced to over 27 years in US for plot to assassinate Trump
stories.summary: A federal judge in Brooklyn sentenced Asif Merchant, 48, a Pakistani national, to more than 27 years for plotting, prosecutors say at the direction of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, to assassinate Trump and other US politicians. Lead with the sentence and what the trial established about the IRGC link, stated as the court's finding and attributed to the DOJ where it is only the prosecution's claim. Explain why it matters now: it lands while the US and Iran are fighting in the Gulf. Dateline Brooklyn.

stories.label: Voyager 1 sets distance record of 1 "light day" from Earth
stories.summary: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now one light-day from Earth: a command sent today takes 24 hours to arrive and the reply another 24. Lead with that round trip. Explain the mechanism that keeps it alive, a plutonium power source losing about 4 watts a year, and the instruments NASA has switched off to stretch it. Merge Ars Technica's reporting on the Golden Record's forgotten details for the human thread. Dateline Pasadena.

stories.label: Rare images of Indigenous group in Amazon highlight threats, advocates say
stories.summary: Rare images of an uncontacted Awá group emerging in Maranhão, Brazil show people whose forest is being cut around them by loggers, hunters and ranchers. Lead with who is encroaching and what Funai's protection of the territory amounts to on the ground. The accountability point: the Brazilian state is legally bound to protect isolated peoples, and the images document how far that protection has slipped. Dateline Maranhão's capital only if the source places it there; otherwise the nearest named town.

stories.label: China accuses Chile and Belgium of ‘backroom deal’ as tensions rise over high seas treaty HQ
stories.summary: The race to host the secretariat of the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ), which governs two-thirds of the ocean, has become a row: China accuses Chile and Belgium of a backroom deal over the headquarters. Lead with the accusation and what each bidder stands to gain. The structural why: whoever hosts the secretariat shapes how marine protected areas and the sharing of benefits from deep-sea genetic resources are run, and a fight now could stall conservation. Dateline Valparaíso if Chile's bid is the frame, else Beijing.

stories.label: Volunteer Dentists, the Revolutionary Guards and Rural Development on Iran’s Home Front
stories.summary: Ground reporting from a village near Shiraz that was evacuated in the March war because it borders an IRGC missile base. The state is now flying in volunteer dentists to treat hundreds of villagers. Lead with that: civilians who live next to a military target, and a government buying their goodwill with clinics instead of moving the base. It is a rare inside view of Iran's home front as the Gulf war widens. Dateline Shiraz.

stories.label: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
stories.summary: A survey of 195 civil-society organisations in more than 68 countries finds that groups which spread their funding across many donors were hit by the global aid retreat anyway. Lead with the survey's hardest numbers: closures, staff cuts and programmes dropped. The mechanism: when the US and European donors cut at once, there is no diversity left to fall back on. Name who loses services in the Global South. Dateline the city the survey's authors work from, or Nairobi if the source centres East Africa.

stories.label: Why isn't Fuel in BiH getting cheaper, despite the Drop in Oil Prices on the Global Market?
stories.summary: Crude has fallen but pump prices in Bosnia and Herzegovina have not, and distributors say why: refining margins have doubled or tripled this year. Lead with that gap. The mechanism, worth teaching: a country that imports refined fuel pays the refiner's margin, not the crude price, so a war-driven squeeze on refining (diesel especially) cancels a cheaper barrel. Who pays: Bosnian drivers and hauliers on some of Europe's lowest wages. Chart Brent crude. Dateline Sarajevo.

stories.label: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
stories.summary: A human brain study finds that the subiculum, a small region at the exit of the hippocampus, encodes where and when an event happened, and that navigation training strengthened episodic memory through it. Lead with the training result: practising finding your way improved memory for life events. Say plainly how many people took part and how large the effect was, and do not overclaim it as a treatment. Dateline the lead authors' institution city.

stories.label: 不到一年！华人“思维链之父”跳槽，Meta的钞能力失效了？
stories.summary: Jason Wei, first author of the 2022 chain-of-thought paper and a builder of OpenAI's o1 and Deep Research, has left Meta's TBD Lab after about a year to become chief scientist at Mercor, an AI training-data and evaluation firm valued at $20bn after a $750m round on 11-10. Lead with the move as a signal: Meta's pay packages did not keep its superintelligence hires, and talent is flowing to the companies that sell data and evaluation. Wei himself says data is 'the next frontier'. Keep the Chinese tech press's framing of Meta's money failing to buy loyalty. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: 英伟达RTX Spark桌面主机首次亮相：最新Demo现场体验，本地AI玩出花
stories.summary: Nvidia showed its RTX Spark desktop in Shanghai, an Arm PC with a Blackwell GPU, a 20-core MediaTek CPU and up to 128GB of memory, built to run AI agents locally. Chinese PC brands begin selling it from 11-18. Lead with Nvidia's own claim that local models now trail cloud frontier models by about two months, down from six to eight. Then the China angle: day-zero support for Alibaba's Qwen and a pitch to Chinese firms on cost and keeping data on-site, with a developer's cloud video-analysis bill as the example. Note the export-control context: this is a chip Nvidia can sell into China. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: Ice hockey governing body website defaced by hackers amid dispute over Russia's exclusion
stories.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation confirmed hackers replaced its homepage with a pro-Russian message attacking Russia's exclusion from international play, just as the IIHF weighs whether to readmit Russia. Lead with the defacement and the timing. The pattern: sports bodies have become soft targets for hacktivist pressure campaigns. Report what the IIHF says was accessed, and attribute nothing to the Russian state unless the source does. Dateline Zurich.

stories.label: What it means if the Houthis take Aden and control the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
stories.summary: After two months of fighting, the Houthis' push on Aden has reached a critical point against Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces. Taking Aden would put both shores of the southern Red Sea approach under one Iran-aligned movement. Lead with what the government stands to lose. The mechanism is geography: whoever holds Aden and the Bab el-Mandeb coast can choke ship traffic through the Strait of Bab el-Mandeb into the Suez route. Name who is paying in Aden itself: civilians, the displaced, a capital-in-exile. Dateline Aden.

stories.label: Why Democrat Mary Peltola's US Senate win in Alaska matters
stories.summary: Peltola's defeat of Dan Sullivan gives the Democrats 56 Senate seats: nine flips, all but one in states Trump carried. Lead with the 56. What a 56-seat majority can and cannot do: it can confirm and block, but the filibuster still needs 60. Name what changes for Trump's agenda, from nominations to war powers, and note Peltola as the first Alaska Native senator if confirmed by the sources. Dateline Anchorage.

stories.label: Marcos flies to China for APEC Summit
stories.summary: Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arrives at the APEC summit in Shenzhen and meets Trump on Xi's ground, days after the Quad's Manila minerals push. Lead with the Philippine balancing act: a US treaty ally at war-adjacent odds with Beijing in the South China Sea attends a summit hosted by China. Use the Trump–Imelda Marcos history only as colour. Name what Manila wants from each capital: tariffs, minerals and security guarantees. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Indian Air Force's Rafale fleet at 32, aviation publication says, backing Pakistan's claim of downing four jets
stories.summary: Flight International's annual fleet estimate puts India's Rafale count at 32, down from 36 before the May 2025 conflict with Pakistan. India has never confirmed losing any. Lead with the missing four: the first independent count that matches Islamabad's claim. The mechanism is accountability through open data: an inventory census does what neither government would. Attribute the estimate to Flight International and give India's position. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: “Pelo menos o banco fez dinheiro”: vazamento expõe bastidores do Deutsche Bank no Brasil
stories.summary: New development in the Deutsche Bank leak, and a Brazilian one: internal files show bank staff played down accusations against Vale, Safra, Braskem and Andrade Gutierrez to keep them as clients. Two of those companies are tied to the Brumadinho dam collapse and the Lava Jato bribery cases. Lead with the quote 'at least the bank made money' and with which allegations were waved through. This is not the Trump-companies angle already covered: dateline São Paulo, about Brazilian clients.

stories.label: Markets should help discipline France over high debt, ECB says
stories.summary: In its financial stability review, the ECB says markets should discipline France and other indebted states through higher borrowing costs, and signals it is in no hurry to step in. Lead with the shift: the central bank that rescued Italy and Spain with 'whatever it takes' is now telling bond markets to do the work. Explain the spread between French and German yields, who pays (French taxpayers, budgets for public services), and how it bears on the ECB interest rate and the euro. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: UK inflation accelerated to 3.6% in October
stories.summary: UK consumer prices rose 3.6% in October, up from 3.5%, and the Bank of England says inflation will climb further. That makes another rate rise likely. Lead with the direction: inflation is accelerating while most central banks are cutting. Name what is driving it (energy pass-through from the Middle East war, food, services) and who carries the cost: mortgage holders and renters. Dateline London.

stories.label: Egypt offers to buy gold from informal miners as it swaps crackdown for licenses | The National
stories.summary: Egypt is abandoning its military crackdown on informal gold miners around Aswan and will now pay them for the gold they hand in, under licences. Lead with the reversal: a state that arrested miners now wants their output, with gold near record prices and Cairo short of dollars. The mechanism is foreign-currency hunger. Raise the IMF's demand that Egypt shrink the state's economic footprint: who captures the margin, the miners or state-linked buyers? Name gold. Dateline Aswan.

stories.label: CISA warns of ‘Java4Shell,’ an AI-found Java bug touching most of the Fortune 500
stories.summary: CISA has issued an emergency patch alert for 'Java4Shell', a Java flaw that lets an attacker take over a server without a password. It touches most of the Fortune 500, and an AI system found it. Lead with the reach and the no-password takeover. The structural point is that AI now finds bugs faster than organisations can patch them, and this lands in the middle of a US outage wave. Give the affected versions and the fix. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: 第一批打工的人形机器人，有的已经失业了
stories.summary: TMTPost reports that some of the first humanoid robots deployed in Chinese factories and shops have already been taken out of service. Lead with which deployments were ended and why: cost, reliability, or tasks a cheaper machine or worker does better. The mechanism: China's subsidy-driven humanoid boom meets the economics of real work. This is the mainland trade-press view of its own hype cycle. Dateline Beijing unless the source names another city.

stories.label: 清华系创企放Vibe Building大招：一句话做AI硬件，2天200元搓出特雷门琴
stories.summary: Moce Intelligence, a 20-person startup from Tsinghua's X-Lab, has released MOCE Designer. From a plain-language request it picks components, wires the circuit, writes and flashes the firmware, and then hands off to JLCPCB for production. ESWIN RISC-V chips are already integrated. Lead with the hackathon theremin built in two and a half days for under 200 yuan. The structural point: 'vibe coding' is moving into hardware, on a Chinese supply chain from chip to factory to JD.com. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Sudden heat spikes harm honey bees more than sustained heat, study finds
stories.summary: A new study finds that a sudden heat shock harms honey bees more than a long heatwave, because the colony adapts as the heat goes on. Lead with the counterintuitive finding: the danger is the first hot day, not the hundredth. Explain the mechanism (heat-shock response, brood temperature control) and what it means for pollination of food crops as heat spikes become more frequent. Name the journal and the institution. Dateline the lead institution's city.

stories.label: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms over West Bank settlements
stories.summary: Britain froze the assets of eight Israeli construction companies that build settlements in the occupied West Bank, and of a settler group that blocks aid trucks into Gaza. Lead with who is named — the firms (Har Hevron among them) and the aid-blocking group — and the mechanism: London is now sanctioning the companies that pour the concrete, not only violent individual settlers. Say what the freeze does and does not reach (UK assets, UK business), and that it lands while Palestinians in Gaza still depend on the aid these groups obstruct. Datelined London.

stories.label: Tamil Nadu Issues Urgent Alert As Cyclonic Storm Akvan Approaches
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan, the third storm to form in the Bay of Bengal in under a month after Arnab and Murasu, is forecast by the India Meteorological Department to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Nellore on November 20, with Tamil Nadu and Odisha on alert. Lead with the landfall date and place, the winds (GDACS Orange, up to 93 km/h) and who must move: coastal fishing communities and the districts under evacuation orders. The structural point is three storms in four weeks hitting the same coast before it has recovered. Datelined Nellore.

stories.label: Companies That Helped Gut EU Climate Law Turn Up for COP31
stories.summary: Members of the 'Competitiveness Roundtable', a secretive coalition of fossil-fuel and heavy-industry companies that lobbied to strip down EU climate law, turned up in force at COP31 while the US government boycotted the talks. Lead with the names of the companies and what each lobbied to weaken in Brussels, then the accountability gap: the firms that watered down the rules now sit inside the room where the next ones are negotiated. Follows our COP31 AI-pledge story, where only nine countries signed. Datelined Antalya.

stories.label: Germany, UK push back after US criticizes Ukraine's deep strikes into Russia
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official questioned whether Ukraine's long-range strikes inside Russia work and warned they harden Russian resolve; Germany and Britain publicly rejected that on November 17. The new development is the open split among Ukraine's backers, days after the Kerch bridge span fell to exactly those strikes. Lead with who said what in Brussels, and the stake: whether Washington's doubts translate into limits on weapons or targeting data that Berlin and London cannot replace. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: US Fed's Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
stories.summary: Fed Governor Lisa Cook, whom Trump has tried to fire since August 2025, told a White House committee through her lawyers that she will not appear at next month's hearing on her removal, calling the process unfair. Lead with the refusal and the mechanism: a president building an in-house tribunal to remove a central-bank governor is a test of whether Fed independence survives, and with it who sets the price of money worldwide. Chart the Fed funds rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Bacolod anti-Pax Silica protest raises alarm over proposed copper mine
stories.summary: A youth-led protest in Bacolod against Pax Silica, the US initiative to lock in supplies of critical minerals and chip technology, turned on a proposed copper mine in Hinoba-an, southern Negros Occidental. Lead with the mine: who holds the permit, how much land and water it takes, and the communities downstream. The mechanism: Washington's push to move mineral supply away from China lands as a mine in a Philippine province, days after the Quad met in Manila on mineral dependence. Datelined Bacolod.

stories.label: 6倍超额认购，Anthropic IPO发行价或再上调！
stories.summary: The new development since our retail-exposure story: Anthropic's IPO book is at least six times oversubscribed (The Information, via Zhidx), so the price could rise from $70–78 to $83–85 a share and the valuation to about $1.5 trillion, pricing due November 19. Lead with the size: 825 million shares, roughly $68–70 billion raised, with Google and Nvidia each putting $10 billion into a parallel placement and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC also buying in. The structural point is that the chipmakers and clouds that sell to Anthropic are also its shareholders. Datelined New York.

stories.label: Waymo temporarily pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
stories.summary: California's DMV banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways after a series of traffic incidents, and Waymo then pulled them off freeways in every US state. Lead with the regulator acting first and the company extending the retreat nationwide, and name the incidents that triggered it. The mechanism: high-speed driving is where a robotaxi's errors are least forgiving, and a state licensing agency, not federal safety law, set the limit. Datelined San Francisco.

stories.label: Huawei’s new sub-brand OSTA set to launch first phone, reportedly featuring Kirin 9030S chip
stories.summary: Huawei's new AI-phone sub-brand OSTA (Xingmang) debuts on November 20, its first handset reportedly running the Kirin 9030S, a chip made in China under US export controls. Lead with the chip: what is known of its process node and who fabs it, and what it says about how far Chinese chipmaking has come despite the ASML equipment bans. Then the strategy: a separate AI-first brand lets Huawei widen its lineup at home. Datelined Shenzhen.

stories.label: AI伴侣的孤独陷阱
stories.summary: A Stanford study of 460,000 real chat logs with AI companions found that for people with weak social networks, the companionship did not relieve loneliness — it deepened it. Lead with that finding and the sample size, and name the study's authors and the measure of loneliness. The mechanism: an always-available companion displaces the human contact the lonely most lack, and the business model rewards more engagement. Datelined Stanford.
